how: Seven throwaway scripts (scratch only, not committed) wrote lines with mentions to pages of the scratch data source with replace_content, then searched each line with update_content in several forms; every page they made was trashed. retrieveMarkdown returns every page mention self-closing: <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/<id>"/>. A database mention comes back with its title: <mention-database url="…">Title</mention-database>.
notes: A mention of a page in the trash was found by its titled form in two probes (from 2 s to 90 s after the trash) and only by its self-closing form in two others: either can be the one.

Twice a titled search Notion otherwise finds was refused: once for a line with two mentions of one page, once for a run of lines after an edit that wrote a broken mention URL. Five later probes repeating both found every titled form. A refused search changes nothing.

cases.case: a page in the database, titled with its current title
the same line as retrieveMarkdown returns it
the title's text without the tag
the part of the line after the mention
a renamed page, titled with its new title
a renamed page, titled with its old title
an untitled page, titled with no title
a page outside the database (a page's child page), also after a rename
a page no one has, which the connection can't tell from one it can't see
the same, titled with no title
a page in the trash, self-closing
a page in the trash, titled

newStr: A mention in new_str may be self-closing or titled (with any title): Notion keeps it and returns it self-closing.
